03 / READ WITH CONTEXT

Clear sources.
Honest limits.

This is an educational collection of AI incidents, related automated-system cases and enforcement controversies. Inclusion does not mean every allegation is proven or every action was deliberate.

Download the full dataset ↗
Download source-review audit ↗
How was AI used to make this project?

AI assisted the research, summaries, checklist writing and website code. Source checks and software tests were performed with AI assistance. This is not independent expert verification. Summaries can contain mistakes; follow the linked originals before relying on a case.

How are sources and their rights respected?

We use short factual summaries and link to the original sources. We do not republish article bodies, third-party incident databases, original photographs, artwork or video. The charts describe our selected records. Source publishers retain rights in their material. Credit is not a substitute for permission where permission is required, and public access is not a reuse licence. No comprehensive legal rights clearance or publisher-specific permission is claimed.

Source selection was updated on 16 October 2026. Individual source checks are dated in the downloadable audit. Sources with unresolved or incompatible reuse conditions are excluded from this published collection; the review download records the selected sources and their conditions. A policy review is not permission or a legal clearance.

The checklists are educational interpretations, not endorsements by the cited organisations. Download the content reuse review ↗

How can I report a correction or rights concern?

Open an issue in the project repository ↗. Include the case or section, the concern and a relevant public source or rights reference. GitHub issues are public: do not post private documents, contact details or other sensitive information. Reports can lead to corrections, attribution changes or removal after review; this is not an automated response service.

Where does the information come from?

Case summaries paraphrase linked official records selected under our source-reuse policy. They are not copied from an incident database. Each case lists its sources, publication dates and the outcome those sources describe.

What do the dates and outcomes mean?

The timeline uses the earliest publication date among the sources cited in each record. The event period is listed separately. “Outcome as of” is the date of the cited outcome, not a claim that the case is still at that stage today. A settlement does not automatically establish an admission. An allegation is not a verdict.

Can these graphs show whether AI harm is increasing?

No. These 30 cases were selected for clear documentation and different lessons. They are not a representative sample. Reporting, language and jurisdiction biases affect coverage. An empty year means no selected records, not no incidents. Jurisdiction describes the source proceeding or affected setting, not necessarily every affected person's location.

How are cases classified and counted?

Every case has one editorial theme so totals do not double count it. Filters and charts count records, not victims, articles or proven violations. Related privacy and marketing practices may belong to the same case. Related data-analytics cases are explicitly labelled; AI marketing claims are not proof of working AI.

How is the collection updated?

This version was reviewed on 16 October 2026. It is manually maintained, not a live feed. Old source outcomes are kept visibly dated. A future update should check both the original account and later corrections, appeals or reversals before changing a record.
